cold.index.ms.small.how: `fathom index` into a deleted store; p95 of the samples. Re-blessed by `reco-3h82` (2026-11-08) at 1 122.5 ms, the middle of what the fleet reads: this container — the class `blessed_environment` describes — gave p95s of 859-879 ms over five `make bench-check` runs of one tree, which is 904-1 034 ms in reference-machine units at that runner's calibration factor of ×0.85-×0.95 (`reco-r3x`'s convention), and the `ubuntu-latest` runner has read 952-993 ms on a fast generation (runs 42382956006, 42370837168, −26 to −29 % against the bless this replaces) up to the 1 341 ms ceiling the two most recent runs cleared without complaint. The number it replaces (1 340.8, blessed at `36b011f`) is now the slow end of the fleet rather than its middle: this box read 1 235-1 341 ms here on 2026-11-07 and 859-879 ms today, while its calibration bench moved only ×0.879 in the same window, so most of the move is work taken off the read path (`reco-7yq` took the graph lane off the commit tables and the analyzers have moved since) that the baseline had never been told about. The floor is 250 ms because the fleet's own spread is that wide — 952 → 1 341 ms is 1.41× on a row whose whole ratchet is ±15 %, and no blessed number reaches both ends from inside ±15 %. What this row can still red on is a move of ~22 %; the 1 500 ms budget guards the rest. Both boxes' readings, and the run each came from, are in this row's own `how`; `tests/test_perf_budget_contract.py::test_the_recorded_fleet_readings_clear_the_ratchet` fails if any of them goes red against this bless. The floor is wider than the ±15 % this row is supposed to resolve, so the gate now lists the id among the ones the ratchet cannot resolve and says `cannot classify` where it used to go red on a machine swap — `reco-dkr`'s confession about the harness, `reco-0zot`'s about a resident set, this row's about the box.

The floor stays `PTY_NOISE_MS` at 10 ms and only the number moved: with 15.441 blessed, the runner sat 10.3 ms away, which is 300 µs outside that same floor, so the job was red on the width of a rounding. Nothing about a 5 ms first paint can be resolved to ±15 % through a pty on any machine; the row stands on the list of ids the ratchet cannot resolve, its 40 ms budget guards it, and the move it can still see is one bigger than its own 10 ms resolution.

rss.tui.mib.small.how: VmHWM of the TUI child, sampled after every keystroke, worst probe. Re-blessed by `reco-0zot` at the median of eighteen probes (three gate harnesses of six) on the class of Linux container `blessed_environment` describes, undivided by any factor because §11.8 forbids scaling a memory row. The number it replaces (30.82, blessed at `36b011f`) was fifteen days and ninety commits old: every runner since has read +15 % past it while the bless box itself had already moved to 33, so the row was a stale number wearing a regression. A floor needs a reason, and this instrument's is not what its name says: at the peak `RssAnon` — the program's own memory — is 15.0-15.2 MiB while `RssFile` is 15.4-18.3 MiB, so over half of `VmHWM` is how much of the 36 MB release binary the kernel had paged in. Measured on one tree on one box: rebuilding it with `-C codegen-units=1` (binary 36.4 → 29.6 MB, `RssAnon` unmoved at 15.0) reads 30.3 MiB against the default build's 33.4, and the GitHub runner reads 35.6-36.9 for a tree this container reads at 33-34. The floor blessed here is 4 MiB for exactly that reason: it is the measured build-and-machine spread of this statistic, not a tolerance chosen to make a red go quiet. What the row can still resolve is a change bigger than ~5 MiB — a leak, not a linker — and a machine inside ±10 % of this bless is inside its own noise.
